periodicity.text: The light curve is dominated by a smooth sinusoid with period 0.27676 d (Lomb-Scargle power 0.61); the adopted 1.10686 d is 4.00 x that. The true period is more likely 0.27676 d (pulsation or spots) or 0.55353 d (contact binary), and the 'eclipses' may not be eclipses.

writeup: TIC 468146715 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 1.1069 days. TESS photometry reveals a primary eclipse causing 1.48% dimming, detected with a signal-to-noise ratio of 65.5 using box least squares analysis. No secondary eclipse was observed. Pixel-level image analysis confirms the signal's origin near the target location, with a difference-imaging peak signal-to-noise of 14.2, though the centroid offset of 1.4 arcsec warrants continued scrutiny. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a novel candidate. The machine learning classifier assigned a score of 0.59 (on a scale where higher values indicate greater likelihood of being a real target), and the data passed all quality checks without flagged issues.
